name: Zainab Noor
title: Instructional Designer, elearning developer
tagline: Hi, Zainab here. I design scenario-based eLearning that closes real skill gaps, so your team performs better and doesn’t just finish a course.
aboutBio:
My journey into instructional design began with graphic design, where I developed a strong foundation in visual communication, hierarchy, and presenting information clearly. I learned how design choices influence the way people perceive, interpret, and engage with information.

As a Presentation Specialist, I began to understand that effective communication goes beyond aesthetics. Organizing content, simplifying complex ideas, and creating a logical flow are essential to helping an audience understand and retain information. This experience sparked my interest in how visual design could support not just communication, but learning.

My experience as a Teaching Assistant brought me closer to the learning process itself. Supporting Adult nursing students helped me recognize that presenting information is only one part of effective learning. Learners also need clear explanations, appropriate guidance, opportunities to engage with concepts, and support in applying what they learn. This experience shifted my perspective from simply designing how information is presented to thinking more intentionally about how people learn.

I carried that perspective into curriculum development for nursing courses, where I began designing learning experiences with a stronger focus on measurable outcomes, instructional sequencing, real world application, and meaningful assessment. Working with course content required me to consider not only what learners needed to know, but also what they needed to be able to do and how their learning could be evaluated. This strengthened my understanding of instructional alignment and the importance of connecting learning objectives, instructional activities, and assessments.

Together, these experiences shaped my approach to instructional design: combining visual clarity with sound instructional thinking to create learning experiences that are engaging, purposeful, and focused on measurable outcomes. I am now looking to bring this multidisciplinary experience into corporate instructional design and eLearning roles, where I can help organizations turn complex information into practical, accessible learning experiences that support employee performance and business goals.
